invariants.rationale: Aggregation is a solver-agnostic process component usable by the single SWAP kernel in standalone and MultiSWAP compositions.
The module contains no files, parsing, paths, units, formats or legacy I/O semantics.
The aggregator receives already-evaluated result records and does not mix immutable parameters, forcing, state or numerical policy into the aggregate result.
The component has no persistent process state.
Aggregation uses only local scalar temporaries and stores no Newton, Jacobian or constitutive scratch per column.
The API uses an assumed-shape ordered level array and imposes no legacy fixed capacity; it can be backed by SoA, pools or batched layouts externally.
Evaluation is pure with respect to committed model state and creates no ledger mutation, so rejected trials leave committed state unchanged.
The stateless O(nlevels) reduction is cheap to repeat from identical per-level responses and has no hidden history.
The component has no day, month, year, midnight or calendar concept.
No coupling-window duration is embedded; aggregation is valid for whichever generic interval produced the constituent responses.
Signed external transfers and aggregate sensitivity availability remain explicit outputs suitable for later coupler composition.
No MODFLOW head, cell or topology semantics are embedded; interface sign and groundwater equality remain responsibilities of the coupling contract.
The total is explicitly a derived view of constituent transfers, invalid fluxes fail closed, and sensitivity failure never deletes valid water flux.
Aggregate dq/dgwl is first-class when all constituent sensitivities are valid; unavailability and singularity are explicit diagnostics.
The reduction is one deterministic pass for flux plus at most one pass for derivatives and requires no extra full SWAP runs.
Dynamic level count and stateless compact records are suitable for many-column batching and do not instantiate heavy solver objects.
The component has no concept of MODFLOW cell fractions or one-to-one tile mappings.
No deep-vadose transfer logic is present; that remains a separate optional component.
Aggregation neither creates nor destroys storage and preserves the signed transfer representation needed for mass-conserving component transitions.
The component consumes generic per-level exchange records and is independent of the particular soil-water solver implementation.
Legacy level-order summation semantics are retained without importing legacy modules, globals or array capacities.
There is no HeadCalc dependency or access to solver-internal arrays.
The aggregator composes physical response metadata only; it contains no relaxation, clipping, smoothing, retry or fallback policy.
Cost is bounded by the supplied level count; invalid inputs fail immediately and no difficult-column iterative path exists inside aggregation.
The frozen B1.10 level-order accumulation remains the reference semantics for qualification; no reference implementation is modified.
Diagnostics expose level count, invalid level, derivative unavailability, nonfinite tangents, branch boundaries, singular tangents and sign composition.
Cost and input storage scale only with the number of active drainage levels supplied to a column; no inactive-option state is allocated here.
Response-law selection, receiver wiring, accepted ledger publication and spatial distribution remain outside the aggregator in runtime/coupler or their owning components.
No implicit midnight, daily-run, .dra, MODFLOW, fixed-MADR or source-sink ordering assumption is present beyond explicit physical level order.
This artifact explicitly evaluates all thirty architecture invariants for the F-PM08C4 change before closeout.
